title: Cortex Watch: Fleet Health & Proactive Burst Dashboard
creator: Oscar Rivera
description: Problem: Operators managing Dedicated GPU fleets lack a single, proactive surface that combines trend-based health signals, scheduled and ad-hoc burst controls, and quick remediation actions. Existing panels are fragmented across Pool Insights, Autoscale settings, and the Incident Timeline. Goal: Design a compact, action-first dashboard (Cortex Watch) that lives in the Console Fleet view and provides real-time health scoring, predictive burst suggestions, one-click remediation, and a drift/rollback quick-path for canary rollouts. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens (desktop + compact mobile view), an interactive prototype for usability testing, annotated component specs for engineering, and an acceptance checklist for PM/Eng handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates the primary flows: view health score, surface anomaly, accept suggested burst, and rollback to previous rollout
Design tokens and spacing match Console system (tokens linked in attachments) and components are annotated with accessibility contrast ratios
Handoff doc lists required telemetry (metrics/events) and minimal API endpoints for actions: suggestBurst, applyBurst, pauseAutoscale, rollbackRollout
Usability sessions (n=5) show users can identify health regressions and trigger a recommended burst within 90 seconds
Edge cases documented: partial pool coverage, multiple concurrent rollouts, and failed burst application with fallback messaging

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Applying burst without capacity checks could cause OOM on nodes. Mitigation: require preflight capacity check endpoint that returns a pass/fail and footprint estimate.
Risk: Cost surprises for customers. Mitigation: inline cost preview and confirmation modal with explicit estimated token/hour change.
Risk: Confusion between automatic autoscale and manual burst. Mitigation: persistent banner showing current autoscale mode and offering a 'snooze autoscale' action when manual bursts applied.
